keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Sultanate). "The article does not describe the territory's boundaries or give an area. It names Mogadishu as the centre"; Merca and Barawa are named as transit stops. A 50 km disc round Mogadishu stands in for a city-state.

ledger.note: Mid-13th century: the sultanate of Mogadishu. "The founding of the sultanate is variously dated to the mid-13th century or 1330"; the infobox says 10th century; founder Abu Bakr bin Fakhr ad-Din, first of the Fakhr al-Din dynasty. 1250 is a placeholder.

region.text: Mogadishu, "the centre"; Merca and Barawa served with it as transit stops for Swahili merchants

ledger.note: Late 16th century: the Fakhr al-Din dynasty ends. "The Fakhr al-Din dynasty ruled up until the late 16th century or start of 1600s" and was replaced by the Muzaffar dynasty; the infobox "disestablished 16th century", "succeeded by Ajuran Sultanate". The year is a placeholder; the Muzaffar clients ruled Mogadishu under the Ajuran and were later dethroned by the Abgaal (Hiraab Imamate).

wars.name: Portuguese attack on Mogadishu
wars.outcome: "In 1542, a Portuguese expedition under João de Sepúlveda attacked the city", which "compelled the sultan of Mogadishu to sign a peace treaty with the Portuguese".

sources.note: Infobox established 10th century, disestablished 16th; founding "mid-13th century or 1330"; Fakhr al-Din dynasty to the late 16th century; Portuguese attack 1542; succeeded by the Ajuran; no extent.

notes: New dossier, thin by necessity: Cliopatria lacks the Sultanate of Mogadishu. One page opened (Sultanate of Mogadishu; budget 1-2). Start (mid-13th century or 1330; the infobox says 10th century) and end (late 16th century, or the start of the 1600s) are placeholders at confidence 1. The page contradicts itself on the Ajuran relation (control 'in the early 13th century' against 'succeeded by Ajuran' and a 1542 treaty the sultan signed alone), so no vassal event is recorded; the Ajuran dossier of this batch notes the same silence. Counterparts: ajuran-sultanate and hiraab-imamate (both written in this batch).
